h1: The 7 Best Laptop Cooling Pads for ASUS TUF, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Cooling Pads for ASUS TUF: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 7 cooling pads for ASUS TUF Gaming laptops, scored on turbo airflow, noise, size range and whether the pad seals to the base.
mainKeyword: laptop cooling pad for ASUS TUF
summary: The IETS GT500 at 5000 RPM is the strongest pad for an ASUS TUF, with a sealed foam collar that sends nearly all its airflow into the base. The llano V12 is the quieter alternative with a dust filter, and the cheaper 4200 RPM GT500 trims noise and cost. Razer suits owners who want automatic speed control, and the Metfut is the silent option for 15.6 inch models only.
intro: TUF laptops are built tough but they are not built cool. Under sustained load the fans spin up, the keyboard deck warms and the clock speeds start to sag, which is the moment a cooling pad earns its place. The trap is buying one that looks powerful but is sized for the wrong chassis: TUF Gaming comes in 15.6 and 17.3 inch versions, and several pads only support up to 15.6.

Our ranking weighs how well each pad delivers air into the base, how loud it gets at full speed and how wide a laptop range it supports. Sealed turbo designs lead because they funnel air where the laptop's own fans pull from. Open multi-fan pads follow, and a silent thermoelectric pad rounds out the list for a very specific buyer.

products.name: IETS GT500 Powerful Turbo-Fan (5000 RPM) Laptop Cooling Pad
products.verdict: The strongest sealed turbo pad here, with speed from 0 to 5000 RPM.
products.description:
The GT500 is a turbofan pad that runs at any speed from 0 to 5000 RPM. A sealed foam collar wraps the airflow path around the laptop base, and a 3-port USB hub gives the TUF's ports a little relief.

That collar is why it leads. Air that leaves the fan has only one place to go, which is up into the intake grille, so the pad's power is not wasted like it is on the open ICE COOREL. The 4200 RPM sibling uses the same design with a lower ceiling, and the llano V12 trades some airflow for a dust filter. The price tier, $50 to $100, is mid-range for what you get.

Buy it if your TUF throttles in long sessions and you game with headphones. The catch is volume: full speed is loud, so most users will run it at half power.
products.idealFor: TUF owners who throttle in long sessions and wear headphones.
products.skipIf: You play near sleeping people or without headphones.

products.name: llano V12 Gaming Laptop Cooling Pad Laptop Cooler Fan Stand
products.verdict: A reinforced pad that supports 15.6 to 19 inch chassis and filters its own intake.
products.description:
The llano V12 uses a 5.5 inch turbo booster fan inside a reinforced frame that takes 15.6 to 19 inch laptops. It plugs into a 36W adapter, carries a 3-port USB hub for peripherals and includes a removable dust filter.

Its chassis range is the reason to pick it for a TUF F17 or A17, since it clears 17.3 inches comfortably, where the Metfut cannot. It sits second because its fan is smaller than the GT500's 5000 RPM turbofan and the airflow figure is less documented, but the dust filter keeps the pad running longer in a dusty room. Against the Razer, it is cheaper and has more USB flexibility.

Buy it if you own a larger TUF and want a pad that lasts. The drawback is that the adapter needs a wall socket, which limits where you can set up.
products.idealFor: Owners of 17 inch TUF models who want a durable, filtered pad.
products.skipIf: You need a portable pad powered through USB alone.

products.name: IETS GT500 Powerful Turbo-Fan (4200 RPM) Laptop Cooling Pad
products.verdict: The same sealed design at 4200 RPM, for less noise and less cost.
products.description:
This GT500 variant runs from 0 to 4200 RPM with the same sealed foam collar sized to the laptop, a bottom intake design and a 3-port USB hub.

It ranks third because the lower ceiling is a fair trade for many owners. A TUF that sits at the edge of throttling does not need 5000 RPM, and 4200 RPM is noticeably quieter at the top end. Against the 5000 RPM model it gives up some headroom, but it takes the sealing benefit intact, which is what the ICE COOREL and ChillCore below cannot match.

Buy it if you want the turbo design without paying for the loudest setting. The tradeoff is that heavy gaming at a 17 inch chassis may justify the extra speed of the 5000 RPM version, so choose by your thermal needs.
products.idealFor: TUF owners who want sealed turbo cooling at lower noise.
products.skipIf: You push a 17 inch model to its thermal limit.

products.name: Razer Laptop Cooling Pad Adaptive Smart, Intelligent Fan Control
products.verdict: A 140mm brushless fan that reads laptop temperature and sets its own speed.
products.description:
Razer's pad has a 140mm brushless fan reaching 3000 RPM inside an airtight foam-sealed chamber, with three magnetic frame sizes and a 3-port Type-A hub. It adjusts speed automatically based on the laptop's temperature.

The automation is what you pay for. A TUF that idles at the desktop and spikes in games gets a pad that follows along, with no knob to turn. It ranks fourth because the 3000 RPM ceiling lags both GT500 models, and the premium tier price, $100 to $200, is steep for that airflow. The magnetic frames help it fit a range of widths.

Buy it if you hate fiddling with fan settings and want quiet by default. The caveat is that cooling per dollar is lower than the IETS pads.
products.idealFor: Owners who want a quiet pad that needs no manual adjustment.
products.skipIf: You want the most cooling for each dollar.

products.name: ChillCore Laptop Cooling Pad, RGB, 9 Fans, 15.6-19.3 Inch
products.verdict: Nine fans and eight height settings across a pad that fits up to 19.3 inches.
products.description:
ChillCore's pad has 9 fans across top and bottom vents, 8 height settings, an LCD fan speed display and 10 RGB light modes. It fits laptops from 15.6 to 19.3 inches, the widest range on this list.

It wins on spread rather than force. Nine fans move a lot of total air across the base and suit a big TUF chassis, but the airflow is diffuse and not aimed at an intake. That puts it fifth, behind every sealed pad, and ahead of the ICE COOREL on fan count, height settings and size range.

Buy it if you own a 17 inch TUF and want cheap, broad cooling with comfortable tilt angles. The caveat: nine fans mean nine bearings to wear, and low-cost fans can get loud as they age.
products.idealFor: 17 inch TUF owners who want low-cost cooling and tilt choices.
products.skipIf: You want the strongest airflow into the intake.

products.name: ICE COOREL Gaming Laptop Cooling Pad, 6 RGB Fans, LCD Screen
products.verdict: Six fans, six angles and a speed display for the lowest price tier.
products.description:
The ICE COOREL has 6 fans spread across top and bottom vents, 6 height settings, an LCD fan speed display, 7 RGB lighting modes and 2 USB ports.

Owners buy it because it is the cheapest route to a real fan array, and it ranks sixth because its fans are smaller and fewer than the ChillCore's nine. The laptop range is not stated as clearly as the ChillCore's, so check it against your TUF size first. Against the Metfut, it moves more air but makes more noise.

Buy it if the TUF is a budget machine and the cooling need is moderate. The caveat is that open fans cannot match a sealed turbo pad in a heavy session, so expect a few degrees of improvement, not a transformation.
products.idealFor: Budget TUF owners who want a fan array and tilt adjustment.
products.skipIf: Your laptop throttles badly in long sessions.

products.name: Metfut Laptop Cooling Pad with Detachable Fan and Cooler
products.verdict: A thermoelectric panel with two fans under 20 dB, for 15.6 inch laptops only.
products.description:
The Metfut takes a different route: a thermoelectric Peltier cooling panel that contacts the laptop base, with 2 fans under 20 dB, a detachable cooler with spring dampers and a carbon steel frame. It supports laptops up to 15.6 inches and 20 lb.

Contact cooling is almost silent, which is its appeal, but it is a smaller effect than a turbo fan forcing air through the intake. That is why it ranks last, along with the 15.6 inch limit that excludes any TUF F17 or A17. For a TUF F15 used in a quiet room, it is a legitimate pick, and it beats the ICE COOREL for noise.

Buy it if silence is your priority and your TUF is 15.6 inches. The caveat: do not expect GT500 level cooling, and check the fit for your exact model.
products.idealFor: 15.6 inch TUF owners who need quiet cooling for study or night use.
products.skipIf: Your TUF is a 17 inch model or you need strong cooling.

methodology.title: Air delivery
methodology.description: Sealed turbo pads that funnel air into the intake ranked above open fan arrays, which spread airflow thin.

methodology.title: Laptop size range
methodology.description: TUF comes in 15.6 and 17.3 inch sizes, so the stated chassis range decided which pads could earn a high spot.

methodology.title: Noise at full speed
methodology.description: We compared stated RPM and decibel figures, since a pad too loud to run helps no one.

methodology.title: Control and convenience
methodology.description: Variable knobs, automatic modes and LCD readouts were credited when they save real fiddling.

methodology.title: Build and upkeep
methodology.description: Frame material, dust filters and replaceable parts decided how long each pad should keep working.

whatMatters.detail: A sealed pad uses a foam collar or pressure chamber so air cannot leak out sideways and must enter the laptop. Open fans just blow at the base. At high loads the difference is large. Look for foam seals or pressure chamber wording in the product details, as on the GT500 and the Razer.

A pad's frame must support the whole base, and a fan placed wrongly misses the intake. TUF models are 15.6 or 17.3 inches, so a 15.6 inch limit excludes the larger ones. Find the stated range in the title or specs, like the ChillCore's 15.6 to 19.3 inch.

RPM measures fan speed, and higher speed moves more air but makes more noise. Some pads list decibel levels too. Choose a variable speed model so you can drop to a quiet setting, and look for 0 to 5000 style ranges rather than a single fixed number.

Pads run on USB power or a wall adapter. USB pads are portable but limit fan strength, while adapters like the llano's 36W allow bigger fans. Check which the listing uses, and remember a USB pad takes a port that your TUF may need for accessories.

Raising the back of the laptop improves typing posture and lets the intake breathe. More height settings give finer control. Look for six to eight settings, as on the ICE COOREL and ChillCore, and check that the pad's rubber grips keep a heavy TUF from sliding.

cards.label: Sealed turbo
cards.text: A single strong fan and a foam collar force air into the intake. It cools harder but is louder. Picks: IETS GT500 (5000 and 4200 RPM), llano V12, Razer.

cards.label: Open fans
cards.text: Many small fans spread gentle airflow across the base. It is cheaper and gentler. Picks: ChillCore, ICE COOREL.

faq.q: Will these pads fit my ASUS TUF?
faq.a: Most support 15.6 inch laptops and several go larger. The llano V12 reaches 19 inches and the ChillCore 19.3, but the Metfut stops at 15.6, so a 17.3 inch TUF needs one of the others.

faq.q: What mistake do TUF owners make with cooling pads?
faq.a: Choosing by fan count. The ChillCore's nine fans cannot match one sealed IETS GT500 aimed at the intake. Compare airflow design and seal first, then count fans.

faq.q: Is the 5000 RPM GT500 worth it over the 4200 RPM?
faq.a: Only if your TUF throttles at 4200 RPM. The 4200 RPM version is quieter and cheaper, while the 5000 RPM model is louder at 65 dB territory, so many players choose the lower speed.

faq.q: How do I set up a turbo-fan pad on a TUF?
faq.a: Line the fan with your TUF's bottom grille, power the pad, and set a low speed first. Raise it only when temperatures climb. The llano V12 and GT500 both let you adjust from a control on the pad.

faq.q: How do I maintain a cooling pad?
faq.a: Wipe blades and vents monthly. Rinse the llano V12's removable dust filter, and use compressed air on the IETS and ICE COOREL. Dust is what shortens the life of cheap pad fans.

faq.q: Does a Peltier pad like the Metfut work better than a fan?
faq.a: No. The Metfut is quiet at under 20 dB, but contact cooling removes less heat than a turbo fan such as the IETS GT500. Pick it for noise, not performance, and only for 15.6 inch laptops.

finalTake: For an ASUS TUF, the IETS GT500 at 5000 RPM is the pad that cools hardest because its foam collar aims every bit of airflow at the intake. The llano V12 is the better pick for a 17 inch model and a dusty desk, and the Razer rewards owners who want automatic control. Check your laptop's size before you buy, because the Metfut only fits 15.6 inch models.
